sentences.text:
State Of A.P., vs Nagala Sanjeeva Rao, on 19 June, 2023
 1
 The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
 Criminal Appeal No.1088 Of 2007
O R D E R:

entities.text: State Of A.P., vs Nagala Sanjeeva Rao
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This criminal appeal is filed aggrieved by the order of acquittal under Sections 420, 465, 468 and 120-B IPC and A-1 is also found not guilty for the offences under Sections 471, 353, 506, 175, 188,
342, 304-A IPC and under Rules 11(1)(vii) and Rule 11(xii) of the A.P. Orphanages and other Charitable Homes (Supervision and Control) Rules, 2001.

entities.text: A.P. Orphanages and other Charitable Homes (Supervision and Control) Rules, 2001
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. It is the case of the CID police that they have conducted inspection in the orphanage being run by accused No.1 and others, there they have found 33 children, who are below three years.

For the reason of not maintaining proper documentation and also violation of the A.P. Orphanages and other Charitable Homes (Supervision and Control) Rules, 2001, the police found that the accused have violated the said criminal provisions and committed acts of cheating fabrication of records etc.

entities.text: A.P. Orphanages and other Charitable Homes (Supervision and Control) Rules, 2001
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. The prosecution in all examined P.Ws.1 to P.W.97 and marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P17 and
in defence accused No.1 was examined as D.W.1 and Exs.D1 to D4 were marked.
The learned Magistrate found that none of the parents of the children have supported the case of the prosecution.

In fact, the child,
who died in the orphanage, the doctor entered into witness box and stated that the child died because of ill-health and nothing to do with A1 to A4, who are running orphanage.
Ex.D4 is the G.O.M.S.No.16 of 2001 which was published on 23.04.2001 and by virtue of which the rules and regulations came into force, regarding maintaining of the orphanages.

4. Learned Magistrate found that the said orphanage was inspected on 20.04.2001 and since the said G.O came into force from 23.04.2001, any violations of the rules will not apply to the orphanage being run by A1 to A4.
Having gone through the evidence, the parents of children stated that the children were given voluntarily for the purpose of adoption as they were unable to maintain the children.
None of the documents which were seized during the course of investigation and marked during trial were proved to be either fictitious or fabricated.

5. In the case of acquittal, the appellate Court can only interfere when there is substantial question of law involved or any compelling reasons or the Court passing orders without considering the evidence on record or contrary to any provision of law.

6. In the present case, the trial Court found that since there were no rules that were framed as on the date of inspection, the question of violation of any of the rules or the consequential penal provisions State Of A.P., vs Nagala Sanjeeva Rao, on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27580046/
1 which were cited were not made out.
7.

entities.text: State Of A.P., vs Nagala Sanjeeva Rao
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said circumstances, the appeal filed by the State fails and accordingly, dismissed.
Miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.

K.SURENDER, J Date: 19.06.2023 sus State Of A.P., vs Nagala Sanjeeva Rao, on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27580046/
